manifest.purpose: Correct planning inputs with unchanged tuning. Historical baseline remains immutable.

allLeaderSchedule.aggregation: Paired by seed and seat; equal weight per leader; report losses and captures, not only yield.

row.name: The Estates
row.flavor: Three orders, one hall, and the hall keeps the minutes.
row.text: Your Economic cards pay 30% more.

row.name: The Curia
row.flavor: What is written in the register is what heaven remembers.
row.text: Your Civic cards pay 30% more.

row.name: Aristotle
row.epigram: He asked what a thing was for, and wrote the answer down.
row.kernel: Founder of the Lyceum; logic, physics, politics, the first library of everything.

row.name: Ptahhotep
row.kernel: The Maxims, the oldest book of advice.

row.name: Phidias
row.epigram: He put his own face on the shield.

row.name: Jang Bogo
row.epigram: No ship was taken while he kept the sea.
row.kernel: A Korean who served as an officer in China, then came home to Silla and built a sea fortress on the island of Wando. He drove the slave raiders from the Yellow Sea and controlled the trade between Korea, China and Japan.

row.name: Ibn Sīnā
row.epigram: Medicine is not hard; the hard part is the patient.

row.name: Āryabhaṭa
row.epigram: The earth turns; the stars do not.

row.name: Murasaki Shikibu
row.epigram: The world is a floating bridge of dreams.

row.name: al-Jazarī
row.epigram: It poured the wine and bowed.

row.name: Marco Polo
row.epigram: I have not told the half.

row.name: Tycho Brahe
row.epigram: A brass nose, and an island for the stars.

row.name: Virgil
row.epigram: So great a labour it was to found the Roman people.
row.kernel: The poet of the Aeneid, the story of how a band of exiles founded Rome, and of the Georgics, a poem about farming.

row.name: Lü Buwei
row.kernel: A merchant who backed a hostage prince as “goods worth hoarding”, put him on the throne of Qin and became chancellor.

row.name: Ibn al-Haytham
row.epigram: Doubt the old books. Then test.
row.kernel: He proved by experiment that we see because light enters the eye, and wrote the Book of Optics. Europe called him Alhazen.

row.name: Hesiod
row.kernel: A farmer poet. Works and Days tells his brother when to plough, when to sail and why to work.

row.name: Widow Qing of Ba
row.epigram: The red stone, and the quicksilver in it.
row.kernel: She ran her family’s cinnabar mines for decades. The First Emperor honoured her and built a terrace in her name. Sima Qian gives her a few lines, and that is all we have.

row.name: War Foundries
row.flavor: The forges run whether the war does or not.
row.text: Towns with a Barracks gain gold equal to 30% of their production.

row.name: The Veterans' Roll
row.flavor: Every name on the roll has served, and the roll grows longer every year.
row.text: +1% science and culture for every rank your units have earned this game, at most +30%.

row.name: Standing Garrisons
row.flavor: The soldiers have been here so long they are townsfolk.
row.text: Per garrisoned unit, the city gains +12% production and +12% culture.

row.name: The Regimental Schools
row.flavor: Between campaigns, the regiment teaches its soldiers to read.
row.text: Each garrisoned unit gives its town +6 science and +6 production.

row.name: The Grand Army
row.flavor: Every regiment sends its reports to the capital.
row.text: Your capital gains +6 science and +6 culture for each military unit you have.

row.name: The Castellans
row.text: Towns gain +6 production for each military and defensive building.
row.flavor: The garrison bought stone from the local quarry.

row.name: The Founders' Rights
row.flavor: The charter has room for another household.
row.text: +3 authority. Cities you found start with one extra citizen.

row.name: Local Clerks
row.flavor: The register is the realm, kept in a smaller hand.
row.text: Gain +3 authority.

row.name: The Old Foundations
row.flavor: The town still uses the halls its founders built.
row.text: Buildings of the first two ages cost no gold upkeep.

row.name: The Builders' Lodge
row.flavor: The builders kept a common book of plans.
row.text: Orders that add yields to buildings pay double.

row.name: The Grain Merchants
row.flavor: The wheat was sold before the barges cast off.
row.text: Towns gain gold equal to 20% of their food.

row.name: The League of Cities
row.flavor: The league is a promise between markets, not between kings.
row.text: Cards that pay your capital also pay your second-largest town.

row.name: The Common Road
row.flavor: A road belongs to whoever is standing on it.
row.text: Your foreign routes give +3 gold, +3 science and +3 culture.

row.name: The Spice Exchange
row.flavor: Pepper bought the ships. The ships bought everything else.
row.text: Every city gains +4% science and +4% culture for each different luxury you hold, at most +32%.

row.name: Money at Work
row.flavor: A full vault builds as surely as a full quarry.
row.text: Every town gains +1 science for every 20 gold you make each turn.
row.note: Your gold income is read after upkeep. Gold that a card pays to your empire as a whole, and not to a town, does not count.

row.name: Bought and Paid For
row.flavor: What was bought stays bought.
row.text: +2% production and culture for each building you have bought with gold, at most +30%.

row.name: The Muda
row.flavor: The galleys sail in convoy, and the state insures the pepper.
row.text: Your trade routes to other empires pay +6 science and +6 culture, and cannot be plundered.

row.name: The Peace of Lodi
row.flavor: The captains went home, and the bankers opened their books.
row.text: While you are at peace, your trade routes pay 50% more. While you are at war, they pay 25% less.

row.name: The Twelve Tables
row.text: Your capital gains +2 production and +2 culture for each Order you hold, seated or not.
row.flavor: A baker dusted the flour from her hands before tracing a line on the bronze.

row.name: Civic Granaries
row.flavor: The stone that marks the square also shades the grain.
row.text: Culture buildings give +1 food and +2 production each.

row.name: The Working Court
row.flavor: Applause is pleasant; the scaffolding it pays for is better.
row.text: Towns with a Monument gain production equal to 30% of their culture.

row.name: The Learned Patron
row.flavor: He funds the study and reads only the dedication.
row.text: Towns with an Amphitheater gain science equal to 30% of their culture.

row.name: The Golden Age
row.flavor: Afterwards everyone agreed it had been one.
row.text: Completing a wonder or gaining a great person gives your cities +25% production and culture for ten turns. A later one restarts the ten turns.
row.note: Gaining another great person or completing another wonder restarts the bonus.

row.name: The Masters' Domain
row.flavor: The estate outlived the man and kept his standards.
row.text: Worked great-person works give +6 food and +6 production.

row.name: The Honoured Dead
row.flavor: The tombs are in the capital because the capital insisted.
row.text: Gains +8 science and +8 production in your capital each time you gain a great person.

row.name: The Wonder Commonwealth
row.flavor: Some towns keep the marvels; the rest keep the memory.
row.text: Towns holding a wonder gain +35% production and food.

row.name: The Prytaneion
row.flavor: Whoever served the city ate at its table, and the city paid.
row.text: Each town gains +1 food for each card you have seated.
row.note: Only the Orders sitting in a chair count, this one included. A charter takes no chair, so it does not count, and neither does a Doctrine.

row.name: The Encyclopedia
row.flavor: Everything known, in order from A to Z, and still not finished.
row.text: Starts at +1 science and +1 culture for your empire. Gains +1 of each every time you gain an Order, complete a wonder or gain a great person.
row.note: Orders from free hands and other cards count. A captured wonder gives no gain.

row.name: The Prefects
row.flavor: One kept the grain coming, one kept the fires out, and one kept the provinces paying.
row.text: +5% production for each Economic card you have seated.
row.note: This card counts itself, and an Economic card in a Wildcard chair counts too.

row.name: The Seven Sights
row.flavor: Travellers came a long way to see seven things, and paid for their supper at every one.
row.text: +5% culture and science for each wonder you hold, at most +30%.

row.name: The Boule
row.flavor: Five hundred citizens, chosen by lot, met on every day the city needed them.
row.text: +2% science and culture for each card you have seated.
row.note: Only the Orders sitting in a chair count, this one included. A charter takes no chair, so it does not count, and neither does a Doctrine.

row.name: The Roll of Masters
row.flavor: Each name on the roll makes the next one easier to find.
row.text: +3% science and culture for each great person you have gained this game, at most +30%.
row.note: A great person counts from the moment you gain it, spent or not. Great people gained before this card was seated count too.

row.name: The Privy Council
row.flavor: The council met in private, so nobody saw how much it decided.
row.text: The cards in your Wildcard chairs pay their yields twice.

row.name: The Polymath's Study
row.flavor: One room, and on its shelves the work of every school.
row.text: Your towns gain +8% science and production for each different deck among the cards you hold, at most +40%.
row.note: Every Order you hold counts, seated or not. A card that two decks share counts for both decks. The cards that belong to no deck count together as one more deck.

row.name: The Pandects
row.flavor: Fifty books of old opinions, cut down to the rules a judge could use.
row.text: +5% science and production for each Doctrine you hold.
row.note: Every Doctrine you hold counts, whatever its deck.

row.name: The Immortals
row.flavor: The ranks never thinned: each guard who fell was replaced before dawn.
row.text: The legacies of your great people count twice.
row.note: A legacy you have lost counts for nothing. A legacy that only allows something gains nothing from counting twice. The cards that count your great people, or their families, still count each person once.

row.name: The Grand Vizier
row.flavor: The vizier kept the sultan's seal, and every order of state passed through the vizier's hands first.
row.text: The card in your first Economic chair pays its yields twice.
row.note: While this card is seated, the council screen names each chair by its place, so you can see which Economic chair is first. Only the yields that card pays your cities and your empire count twice. Its bonuses on hexes, its percentages, the yields it pays as a share of another yield, and its rules do not. A loss of gold on that card counts twice too. If the chair is empty, or your government has no Economic chair, this card does nothing.

row.name: The Processional Way
row.flavor: The road from the Ishtar Gate ran straight through Babylon, between walls of blue glazed brick and rows of striding lions.
row.text: Hexes beside two or more great-person works give +10 culture and +10 science.

row.name: The Stele of Deeds
row.text: You have one more Wildcard chair for every three wonders you hold, at most two more.
row.flavor: The carver left room at the foot of the stone for the names still to come.

row.name: The Arthashastra
row.flavor: A king has no friends, only offices, and the manual lists them all.
row.text: You have one more Wildcard chair. The card seated in it counts twice.
row.note: This is the last Wildcard chair of your council that no malice holds, and the council screen marks it. If you gain another chair, or a malice takes this one, the mark moves. The card's yields, percentages, combat lines and riders all count twice. A rule that is simply on or off holds once, and the card opens no second chair.

row.name: The Magnaura
row.flavor: The palace pays the masters, and the masters train the palace.
row.text: Each town gains +2 science for each Civic card you have seated.

row.name: The Jinshi
row.flavor: Thousands sit the examination, and a handful are presented.
row.text: You have two more Civic chairs.

row.name: The Barmakids
row.flavor: The vizier's house fed poets, physicians and the first paper mill.
row.text: Each great person you have gained gives every town +1 food and +1 production.

row.name: The Council of Ten
row.flavor: Set up for one emergency, and never once dismissed.
row.text: You have two more Wildcard chairs.

row.name: Scutage
row.flavor: Those who stayed at home still paid the crown.
row.text: Orders you hold but have not seated pay half their yields. You have one fewer Wildcard chair.
row.note: Off its chair, a card pays half of its flat and counted food, production, gold, science, culture and faith. Its costs do not follow it, and neither do its percentages, combat lines, riders, rules or commissions. Its happiness, authority and renown pay nothing, and a charter pays nothing. It counts what it would count in a chair, and a card that grows pays half of what it has banked. Your last Wildcard chair closes at once, and a card seated there returns to your collection.

row.name: The Union of Lublin
row.flavor: A king, a senate and a chamber of envoys, and each was sure it ruled.
row.text: You also gain the abilities of the other two governments of your tier.
row.note: Your chairs are still your own government's. If you adopt a government of a new tier, you gain the abilities of the other governments of that tier instead.

row.name: The Laboratories
row.flavor: Each school kept a workshop for its instruments.
row.text: Science buildings give +10% production.

row.name: The Secret Arts
row.flavor: What the workshop knows, the workshop keeps.
row.text: Each town gains +1 production for each technology you know that no empire you have met knows, charter technologies included, at most +5.

row.name: The Roll of Scholars
row.flavor: Each name on the roll brings more students to the halls.
row.text: +4% production and culture for each great scholar you have gained this game, at most +28%.

row.name: The Humanists
row.flavor: They read the old poets and write new ones.
row.text: Towns with a Library gain culture equal to a quarter of their science.

row.name: The Pythagorean Brotherhood
row.flavor: All is number, and the numbers are kept inside the temple walls.
row.text: +2 science in every city, doubled in cities with a Shrine.

row.name: The Two Capitals
row.flavor: One court in the north and one in the south, and a ministry for each.
row.text: Your largest town besides your capital also counts as your capital for your cards. Your other towns grow 25% more slowly.
row.note: Only your Orders and Doctrines count the second town. Wonders, governments, beliefs, leaders, great people, luxuries and building sites still mean your true capital. The largest town is read again each time, so another town can take its place, and the older town keeps a tie. Neither capital grows more slowly. A one-time gift still lands in your true capital. The palace and authority do not change.
